title: Reconcile current Math README and delivery guide while preserving historic DWF source pins
commitMessage: docs: reconcile current Math README with qualified local delivery

contribution.summary: Reconcile dw.tools.math's public README with durable post-M7 local delivery truth, preserving immutable historical DWF source pins. Replace the initial-planning front-page claim with verified 13-package/7-consumer/95-probe status, add practical local-only package guidance and independently check that the dated 2026-10-07 snapshot is retained solely as an archive. No publication, product changes or new milestone.
contribution.value: The bounded RS130 documentation run installs a new README, a verified thirteen-package consumption guide, a provenance decision and a read-only C# verifier. The validator checks RS129 attempt 001 first-pass success, its source-pinned five-report portfolio, unchanged historical RS124 checker bytes, one archived original README sentence, all 541 completed nodes, unsent coordination requests and Discovery nonclaims. Historical inventory and portfolio checkers are run again as validations, without editing their SHA-pinned files or any prior receipt.
debtChanges: Historical RS124/RS129 checkers retain their original dated README string as an archived anchor; prior receipts remain immutable historical observations.
The 13 locally packed preview packages, 7 source-free client executions and 95 probes do not prove public release, ABI compatibility or another RID.
Math Discovery skill and actual CLR broker bindings remain candidates; future stage B must qualify them, not advertise them prematurely.
AURA/Decision/MCDM requests are drafts only. Stage D permits review/preparation, not unauthorized outward transmission.
No change to accepted backlog 0.1.122 or the 541-node native DWF plan; RS130 has zero completion achievements.
contribution.nextAction: On confirmed RS130 push, prepare the already owner-approved next stage B: a separately bounded Math dw.discovery/AURA qualification, verifying supported DWF planning, portable protocol evidence and genuinely callable APIs.
